summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, chronic diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and diabetes presented with substernal chest pressure during hemodialysis, associated with hypotension. The pain lasted approximately two hours and resolved with fluid resuscitation. She remained asymptomatic in the hospital. Workup showed no acute EKG changes and stable cardiac enzymes, with troponin elevation likely attributable to chronic kidney disease. She was managed conservatively without intervention, remained in sinus rhythm, and was discharged on her prior medications. The chest pain was attributed to hypoperfusion during dialysis due to her preload-dependent state. Discharge instructions emphasized weight monitoring, fluid and sodium restriction, and prompt evaluation for recurrent symptoms.
